blocks.text: The INN NEWS - elections are an important moment in democratic life. As a rookie voter, you have a crucial role in deciding the future of the country.
In Indonesia, the age of a rookie or minimum-age voter to be listed as a electoral vote is 17 years.
In accordance with the 2017 Number 7 Act on Election, one can register as a voter by the time they're 17 or more at the time of the election.
However, they can only vote in the next election after they're 17.

The elections in 2024 will be your first chance to participate in the democratic process. To help you face those elections, this is a guide that will give you insight into how you can prepare yourself and make wise decisions.
Political Education

One of the first steps that's important is to acquire enough political knowledge. Take the time to understand the political system, different political parties, and important issues that become focused in elections.
Read the news, follow the public debate, and use the online resources available to further your understanding of the issues.
Chooser Registration

Make sure you're listed as a voter. Check if you've been listed as a voter in your residential area. If not, find out the registration procedure and make sure you sign up with enough time before the elections.
Normally, the Public Election Commission would give information about the voter registration process.
Party and Candidate Compliance
Do the comparison between a political party and a candidate who competes in elections. Review the programs and the platforms they offer.

Note the visions, missions, and scores they propose. This comparison will help you understand the difference between a political party and a candidate and determine your options based on your values and issues that are important to you.
Consider Main Issue

The primary identification of the issues that you consider important in elections. For example, economics, education, environment or health. Know where each political party and candidate stands on those issues. Consider the implications of their policy to those issues and see if their approach corresponds to your values.
Join the public debate
The public debate can give more insight into candidates and their views on important issues. Follow the debate held by political parties or debates held by the media.
Listen to the arguments that are delivered and consider those arguments when making your decisions.
Use Available Resources
Use online resources like KPU websites, research agencies, and civil society organizations that provide information regarding elections.
They often provide profiling candidates, political appeal parties, and industrial analysis of important issues. By exploiting this resource, you can make more informative decisions.
Keep Independent and Critical
Always maintain dependency and critical in processing information. Avoid the influence of propaganda or narrative that can affect your thinking without strong basis.
Evaluate carefully the sources of information you receive and check for facts before making decisions.

As a novice vote in the 2024 elections, you have an important role in shaping the future of the country. With adequate political education, careful research, and critical thinking, you can face these elections with confidence.
Use this guide as a basis to prepare yourself and make a wise decision when you choose to. Remember that active participation in the democratic process is the first step towards positive change.
